conviction_note: The findings sum to -0.2, and I emit -0.1 because the one negative (raw potato supply on both continents falling short of what the July guide assumed) points the same way as the -20.7% 20-day run-up and four target cuts in the last week, so most of it is probably already in the price; the reported-quarter beat that is likely has not paid on this name in the last three prints; this is close to an honest zero, and the print will turn on the FY27 guide and the North America contracting update, which I cannot call from documents.
bar: Q1 FY27 adjusted EPS $0.58 (Zacks via ad-hoc-news, https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/lamb-weston-stock-heads-into-earnings-after-target-cut/70196124) and $0.59 (MarketBeat/DefenseWorld, https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/09/29/lamb-weston-lw-expected-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday.html); revenue consensus $1.66B. These agree with the company's own Q1 guide on the 2026-07-24 call: net sales flat (Q1 FY26 was $1,659.3M) and adjusted EBITDA down low teens from $302.2M, so roughly $260-266M (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-lamb-weston-tops-q4-2026-estimates-as-volume-rises-93CH-4812068). On 2026-08-12 the CFO guided Q1 gross margin to 'the low 18% range' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/lamb-weston-at-bank-of-america-smid-cap-virtual-conference-margin-reset-93CH-4855539). FY27 guide: EPS $2.95-3.25, adjusted EBITDA $1.1-1.2B, net sales +0-1% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001679273/000167927326000024/a-lwx20260531xexx991fy26v2.htm). print_vs_bar_pct is on adjusted EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest is not crowded. FINRA settlement 2026-08-31: 6,294,922 shares short, 4.77 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/lw/short-interest). ORTEX, 2026-09-30: 4.7% of free float, borrow cost 0.48%, availability 2,455% of short interest (https://ortex.news/articles/177222/lamb-weston-heads-into-earnings-with-options-traders-at-peak-caution). MarketBeat, 2026-09-30: 4.90% of float, up 5.8% (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-jpmorgan-chase-co-has-lowered-expectations-for-lamb-weston-nyselw-stock-price-2026-09-30/). The baseline has no skew: the chain is unusable, and the open-interest put/call of 8.43 rests on 66 contracts, so it means nothing. ORTEX puts the volume put/call at 2.08, near its 52-week high of 2.16, against 0.63 in mid-September. Options traders are buying downside protection into the print, the stock is down 20.7% over 20 days, and the short base is small.

findings.finding: Since the 2026-07-24 FY27 guide, the potato crop has come in well short on both continents. On that call management assumed 'an average crop' in Europe, and on 08-12 the CFO said FY27 EBITDA growth comes 'mainly from the international business'. NEPG now puts north-west Europe's crop down about 25%, the smallest in decades. Idaho is heading for its smallest crop since 2011, with yields 'as bad as we've had in years', low specific gravity, smaller sizes and open-market prices the highest since summer 2023 (Capital Press and FreshPlaza, 2026-09-29). Both raise the risk that the FY27 range is trimmed or pinned to its low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This stock moves on guidance. The 2024-12-19 guide cut fell 20.1%. On 2025-12-19 a beat whose guide implied a large H2 profit decline fell 25.9%. On 2026-04-01 a beat with a narrowed guide fell 8.9%. The 2025-07-23 FY26 guide with cost savings rose 16.3%. The 2026-07-24 guide modestly above consensus traded up 6.8% intraday and closed +0.81% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The European half is priced. Stephens cut its target on 09-28 explicitly on the European crop, JPMorgan cut on 09-30, and the stock is down 20.7% over 20 days, so a European-crop miss would show up as no further decline. The Idaho half is two days old, and none of the analyst notes I found cites it. If it were priced, North American procurement risk would sit in the bear case, and it does not.
findings.independence: The European crop figure comes from a separate source: NEPG via UkrAgroConsult (https://ukragroconsult.com/en/news/smaller-area-and-drought-to-cut-europes-potato-crop-by-a-quarter/). The independent counter-evidence is why this is sized small. DCA's Ramaker (https://www.potatonewstoday.com/2026/09/25/eu-4-potato-production-set-to-fall-by-almost-a-quarter/) says processors are shielded because they locked contracts 15-25% lower, and the growers bear the shortfall. The CFO said Europe is 'mostly contracted' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/lamb-weston-at-bank-of-america-smid-cap-virtual-conference-margin-reset-93CH-4855539). On the same call he said real input inflation strengthens LW's hand in pricing talks, which could turn a short crop into firmer price/mix. Washington, LW's largest sourcing region, was reported in good condition in June (https://www.agwestfc.com/education-and-resources/industry-and-economic-insights/industry-insights/potatoes), but nothing dated later. These offsets are netted into the one sign here, not filed as a separate positive.

findings.finding: The Q1 bar is management's own explicitly low guide: net sales flat, EBITDA down low teens, gross margin around 18%. Consensus EPS of $0.58-0.59 sits on it. LW beat EPS in each of the last four quarters by wide margins ($0.87 vs $0.62 in Q4, $0.72 vs $0.63 in Q3). The one peer print after LW last spoke, Conagra on 2026-09-30 for the June-August quarter, showed foodservice up 3.2% and reaffirmed its guidance. That makes an in-line-to-beat print the likely reported quarter, even with QSR traffic down 3.4% in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have not been paid. The 40% EPS beat on 2026-07-24 closed +0.81%. The beat on 2026-04-01 fell 8.9%. The 'decent beat' on 2025-12-19 fell 25.9%. Only the 2025-09-30 beat with a reaffirmed guide rose (+4.33%).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The guide is public and consensus already sits on it. What is left is the habit of beating, which the street has seen four times. If it were fully priced, previews would carry a whisper above $0.59, and none that I found does.
findings.independence: Conagra's Q1 FY27 foodservice +3.2% (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9103281/conagra-brands-cag-reports-q1-revenue-slightly-above-estimates-reaffirms-fiscal-2027-guidance) points the same way. Pointing against it: Placer.ai QSR traffic -3.4% YoY in August (https://www.qsrweb.com/news/restaurant-traffic-moderates-but-qsrs-remain-above-2026-average/) and McDonald's Q2 US comps +0.8% with guest counts down (https://corporate.mcdonalds.com/corpmcd/our-stories/article/Q2-2026-results.html). LW's FY26 volume growth came from share gains rather than traffic.

outside_window.finding: The frozen-potato price-fixing class action (In re Frozen Potato Products) survived the motion to dismiss with DOJ support, and a shareholder class action also survived dismissal. No settlement or trial date falls inside the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Event confirmation: the company's IR release confirms results 2026-10-06 at about 8:00 a.m. ET, call at 9:00 (https://investors.lambweston.com/news-releases/news-release-details/lamb-weston-announce-fiscal-year-2027-first-quarter-financial), so the event is real.

EDGAR since 2026-07-01: the 8-K of 07-15 is an inducement-plan share reduction; the 8-K of 09-16 is item 5.07 (annual meeting); the S-8 of 09-23 follows the plan; the Form 4s on 08-05 are seven filers on one day, consistent with director grants, not open-market buys. Nothing quiet or new.
Plant closures, layoffs or curtailments in Aug-Sep 2026: none found (the Connell and Munro items are 2024 and 2026-01).
Activist or strategic news (Jana, Continental Grain, Post Holdings) in 2026: nothing new beyond the stakes ORTEX cites.
European open-market (Belgapom) prices for September 2026: no dated figure found, only the spring 2026 zero quotes.
Columbia Basin processing yields for the 2026 harvest: no dated post-June report found. The USDA AMS report of 09-18 is fresh-market only.
Edible oil: soybeans +27.6% and canola +35% YoY at 09-30, but only +1.4% over the month and already guided as 'biggest inflation driver', so not new.
McCain and Simplot results or pricing actions: nothing public.
baseline_tension: The one negative agrees with the -20.7% 20-day run-up, the -37% from the high, the elevated put volume and the wave of target cuts, so most of it is likely priced. With no usable skew and a small, cheaply borrowed short base, nothing in positioning argues for sizing it larger.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (documents beat inference; macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis): the crop finding reasons from weather. For Idaho, neither the company nor a direct counterparty has said what it does to LW's cost, and DCA plus the CFO say European processors are mostly contracted. Cut from -1.0 to -0.5.

Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest): Idaho is part of North America, and Washington, the largest sourcing region, had good early reports. This also supports the smaller crop size and the wider upside band (+2.0).

Lesson 1 (the reaction function has veto power): the last three beats closed at +0.81%, -8.94% and -25.94%. Cut the reported-quarter finding from +0.5 to +0.3 and kept print_vs_bar at +4.0, so the two numbers diverge on purpose.

Lesson 3 (the caveat has to reach the number, and one sign per entity): the short crop is evidence both for higher cost and for firmer pricing, so I kept it as one netted finding and did not file a separate pricing-power positive. Because the negative agrees with the run-up, expected_move_pct is set at -0.1 against a sum of -0.2.

Lessons 6 and 7 left standing: the bar is sourced to the company guide and two agreeing estimate sources, so no cap applies; short interest was checked before the negative and is not crowded; there is no skew to go against.
